storage: append-only JSONL day-files under <archive>/faastatus/ by CAPTURE date (gz after 2 days)
written_by: server/faaStatus.ts archiveFaaEvents (15-min poll — delay programs are intraday phenomena; eager boot)
source: FAA National Airspace System status (nasstatus.faa.gov/api/airport-status-information) — keyless XML; ground stops, ground-delay programs, arrival/departure delays, closures. Shape verified live 2026-07-05 (thunderstorm day fixture)
license: US government work, public domain; attribution 'FAA National Airspace System Status'

field_map.type|airport|reason|numbers — dedup key: the feed is a rolling snapshot, not an event log: a program persisting across polls archives ONCE; when its published numbers change, the new state appends vintage-style
field_map.avg/max/min/end_time/reopen/trend: as published, human-readable strings ('2 hours and 30 minutes') — NOT normalized to minutes at capture; normalization is analysis-time work so the raw record stays faithful
field_map.duration honesty: the feed carries no clear/cancel times — program durations are LOWER BOUNDS reconstructed from our capture times, never inferred beyond that
field_map.update_time/rt: feed's own Update_Time + as-seen UTC timestamp

confidence_model: RAW official operational status. Empty NAS (zero programs nationwide) is a real publishable state, cached and served as such. HYPOTHESIS (gate-locked): sustained delay-program frequency at cargo hubs (MEM/SDF/CVG/ANC) as a parcel-carrier cost-pressure indicator — prior ~20% (weather dominates and is priced); the archive is cheap and honest RAW value regardless.
geo_fields: (airport IATA/FAA code -> coordinates needs an airport table; map layer deliberately deferred)
cadence: 15-min poll (96 light requests/day) so intraday program churn lands in the archive
_note: Universal archive envelope (approved 2026-07-04). BUILD ORDER 5 #4; XML parsed regex-per-edgarForm4-precedent with a prefix-boundary fix (<Delay> vs <Delay_type>) that the EDGAR helpers never needed.
